properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued August 5 at 12:07PM EDT until August 5 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
SMWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20
NM...

* Until 100 PM EDT.

* At 1207 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms producing waterspouts were
located along a line from near Charleston Harbor Entrance to near
Kiawah Reef, moving north at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Lowcountry Anglers, Air Force Reef, Charleston Nearshore Reef,
Charleston Coastal Anglers, Kiawah Reef, Rattlesnake Shoal, Joe
Shuford Reef, Charleston Sixty, N. Edisto Nearshore Reef, Capers
Island Buoy and Deveaux Bank.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
properties.area: Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20 NM

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued August 5 at 9:57AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 10:56AM CDT until August 7 at 11:43AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 6.3 feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.9
feet on 06/15/1986.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 5 at 11:55AM EDT until August 5 at 3:00PM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
FFWLWX

The National Weather Service in Sterling Virginia has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Baltimore County in northern Maryland...

* Until 300 PM EDT.

* At 1155 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1
hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Baltimore...                       Sparrows Point...
Dundalk...                         Essex...
Rosedale...                        Edgemere...
Turners Station...                 Eastpoint...
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 5 at 11:53AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal waters from Murrells Inlet to South Santee River SC out 20
NM...
Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20
to 60 NM...

At 1153 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was
located near C J Davidson Wreck, moving northeast at 15 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes. If caught on the open water,
prepare for deteriorating conditions. Make sure you and your crew are
wearing properly fitted life jackets.

This storm may produce a waterspout. A Special Marine Warning may be
needed.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Murrells Inlet to South Santee River SC out 20 NM; Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 5 at 10:00AM CDT until August 5 at 1:15PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
At 1000 AM CDT, delayed spotter reports were received of flash
flooding in the Murray area in western Clarke County around 840 am,
with more than six inches of water flowing over some roads, where
the heaviest rain occurred. Although floodwaters are likely on their
way down, flash flooding remains possible especially in lower areas
or areas small streams and other drainage areas.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Osceola, Corydon, Lakeside Casino, Murray, Seymour, Allerton,
Humeston, Van Wert, Garden Grove, Woodburn, Weldon, Derby,
Millerton, Le Roy and Murray Roadside Rest Area.
properties.instruction:
For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
properties.area: Clarke, IA; Decatur, IA; Lucas, IA; Wayne, IA

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Des Moines IA has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in Iowa...

Thompson River at Davis City affecting Decatur County.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...The Thompson River at Davis City, or from the City of
Grand River to the Iowa-Missouri border.

* WHEN...From this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Water affects the Davis City park and
campgrounds.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached based on the latest

properties.instruction:

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

River forecasts include observed precipitation plus forecast
precipitation over the next 24 hours.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 4:18AM AKDT until August 5 at 5:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Petersville Area

* WHEN...Until 500 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated scattered rain showers continue across the warned
area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts of up to 0.5 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 4:18AM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing. Trees and debris larger
than telephone poles have been observed flowing down the
river. Between 1.0 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of up to 0.5 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 3:50am the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: Cresting Wednesday morning above 22 feet.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
